free_tier.stated: Cloudflare for Startups gives early-stage companies up to $350k in credits to build the next big idea ... Get started with $10k in credits to build and launch your product, no minimum funding required.

egress.terms: the $10k tier carries no byte allowance of its own because Cloudflare's developer platform has no metered egress to spend it on; ingress: http-only

tooling: wrangler and the Cloudflare API; no VM is involved
chaining: composes with a free VM elsewhere rather than replacing it: the credit buys Workers and R2, not an ingress port

limits.value: a company application, with the tier set by amount raised

binding_note: two things fail before volume: the applicant must be a company, and the credit spends only on Cloudflare products, which already carry no egress meter. There is nothing for 1 TiB a month to run out of.

identity_cost.detail: early-stage companies, with the tiers set by funding stage: 'Under $1M raised' for the $10k tier and 'Under $5M raised' for the $100k tier

reliability_note: credits are tied to programme membership and expire with it
confidence_note: the tier structure is first-party and read; whether a sole founder with no entity can apply is not stated

evidence.proved: 'up to $350k in credits', 'Get started with $10k in credits ... no minimum funding required', 'Under $1M raised', 'Credits: $10k', 'Under $5M raised', 'Credits: $100k'

notes: Recorded to close the route rather than open it: Cloudflare's egress is already free on R2 and on Workers, which is why a credit there is worth less than it looks for this question. The $10k tier is reachable without funding in principle but needs a company.

extras.wg_detail: Cloudflare sells no VM; the credits spend on Workers, R2 and the rest of the developer platform, none of which hands a user a UDP port on a public IPv4
extras.volume_stated: the $10k tier carries no byte allowance of its own because Cloudflare's developer platform has no metered egress to spend it on
extras.transit_note: Cloudflare carries the bytes on its own network, which is the part that is already free
